Ragtime Annie

An American fiddle tune which has been very much a standard for American squares and running sets. The notation here is not quite as generally played. Herewith my ABC for the tune:

Strickly old-time

I’ve played this tune for years, but only in old-time circles. Never, ever heard it played at a session, and I suspect that anyone who would dare start this tune at a session would get some serious stink-eye from the others.

↳ Posted by fcmaynard on May 24th, 2017.

Re: Ragtime Annie

Just wondered if it is played as straight as written, or maybe with a bit more swing and suspicion of dottedness? (Also thinking of Pig Ankle Rag, for which we were given a very “straight” score but then told play it more syncopated.)

↳ Posted by trish santer on May 27th, 2017.

Re: Ragtime Annie

Trish Santer the local old time folk music group whom I play my acoustic string bass with likes to play “Ragtime Annie” with some swing and syncopation and suspicions of “dottedness”. In all of the years I have been playing music with this group of mixed up mixed nuts, I don’t think I have ever heard anyone play “Ragtime Annie” straight with no swing like a reel. We play “Pig Ankle Rag” the same way with some swing and and syncopation and “dottedness” instead of playing it straight. However, after playing ragtime music since I was a teenager and listening to musicians who play ragtime professionally, I can and will testify that ragtime is supposed to be syncopated and is supposed to be played with its own type of “swing” but not like jazz.
Does this help?

Laurence
